06/ Dated 07.07.2025 I.A. No. 7435 of 2025 Heard Mr. Randhir Kumar, learned counsel for the appellant No.1 and Ms. Snehlika Bhagat, learned A.P.P on behalf of the State.
This interlocutory application has been preferred by the appellant No.1 for grant of bail to him during the pendency of this appeal.
The appellant No.1 has been convicted for the offences under Sections 304B/34 and 498A/34 of the Indian Penal Code and has been sentenced to undergo R.I. for 14 years for the offence under Sections 304B/34 of the Indian Penal Code.
It has been submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant No.1 that the other co-convicts have been granted bail by this Court.

It has further been submitted while referring to the evidence of the informant, who has been examined as P.W.2 that he has categorically stated that the deceased was burnt to such an extent that she was not in a position to speak.

sentences.text: Learned A.P.P on behalf of the State has opposed the prayer for bail of the appellant No.1 and has submitted that appellant No.1 is the husband of the deceased and there is consistent evidence that he used to torture and commit assault upon the deceased.
It has further been submitted while relying on the evidence of P.W.2 that it is the appellant No.1, who has primarily responsible for setting ablaze his wife.
The cross-examination of P.W.2 categorically reveals that his daughter was not in a position to speak because of the burn injuries suffered.
This statement itself dilutes Exhibit-7 as well as the allegation of the appellant No.1 being involved in setting ablaze of the deceased.
Regard being had to the above, we are inclined to admit the appellant No.1 on bail.

Accordingly,
during the pendency of this appeal, the appellant No.1 is directed to be released on bail, on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- (Rs. Ten Thousand) with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned Additional Sessions Judge-II-cum-Special Judge, FTC (Offence against Women), Koderma, in connection with Sessions Trial No.53 of 2020 & S.T. No.58 of 2021.
The aforesaid I.A. stands allowed and disposed of.

(Rongon Mukhopadhyay, J.) (Ambuj Nath, J.) BS/-
